title: An international commitment can be formally reported while congressional and public visibility arrives late or incomplete
source_unit: GAO-26-108186 review of State Department reporting and publication of international agreements and qualifying nonbinding instruments
geography: United States executive-branch international commitments; reporting and publication between October 2023 and March 2025, with website review through April 2026

observations.period: October 2023-March 2025 reporting; website status as of July 2025 and April 2026

denominator.unit: international agreements and qualifying nonbinding instruments State reported to Congress, excluding classified items from the timeliness analysis

reported_on_time.unit: agreements and instruments reported to Congress

reported_late.value: 90 of 311 were late at one or both reporting points; late items averaged 2.3 reporting cycles late
reported_late.unit: agreements and instruments reported to Congress

public_publishing.value: an estimated 86% of items subject to publication requirements had text and legal-authority information published

public_publishing_on_time.value: an estimated 53% met the 120-day publication deadline; instruments were estimated at 78% and agreements at 38%
public_publishing_on_time.unit: estimated rate among items subject to publication requirements

discoverability.value: text and legal-authority information were spread across webpages with different designs and identifiers, and users often had to know dates or identifiers to locate and match records

commitment_effect.value: not observed as a common implementation, partner, burden-sharing, legitimacy, or changed foreign-behavior outcome

observations.method: GAO audited State reporting and publication against the Case-Zablocki Act, regulations, and federal internal-control standards; it analyzed 311 reported items, a generalizable publication sample of 156 items, agency and Treaty Office processes, and website discoverability.
observations.uncertainty: The 311-item timeliness frame excludes classified items and reflects State's reported universe. Publication estimates have sampling uncertainty and statutory exemptions. Late or hard-to-find information does not by itself establish concealment, bad faith, invalid commitments, or lack of congressional awareness through other channels.
observations.subgroup: International agreements versus qualifying nonbinding instruments; State bureaus and offices and more than 100 potentially reporting federal agencies; classified and exempt instruments follow different visibility routes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reporting and publication can be delayed by translation, diplomatic notes, physical documents, classification, legal review, administrative errors, or uncertainty about whether an instrument qualifies. A searchable public record may improve oversight without changing the underlying commitment or partner behavior.

related_sources.claim: GAO report landing page and official PDF metadata identify the June 2026 audit and recommendations.

boundary: This record measures reporting timeliness, publication completeness, and discoverability for selected international commitments. It does not establish commitment quality, implementation, partner consent, legitimacy, strategic effect, or executive intent.
